newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya Power posts marginal profit rise.
newsitem.headline: Kenya Power posts marginal profit rise.

text.p: Power monopoly Kenya Power & Lighting Co has posted a marginal profit and doubled its dividend and bonus offers, officials said.

It posted a profit of 1.116 billion shillings ($20.42 million) after tax for the year to June 30 1996 from 1.082 billion shillings in the year to June in 1995, a company statement passed to the Nairobi Stock Exchange showed.

The company, in the statement on Thursday, said it would issued a dividend of 8.0 shillings and a bonus of two shares for every one held compared to 4.0 shillings and one share for one in the previous financial year.
Kenyan companies routinely announce their results months after the close of their financial year.
Financial analysts said the expansion of the company's capitalisation base was part of it's efforts to raise funds for its ongoing restructuring programme.
Last week, the company confirmed that it would separate it's generation and distribution functions, which would leave it as the sole distributor of electricity in Kenya.
"It will turn to a proper service concern as opposed to an industrial firm," said a market analyst from investment advisers Loita Asset Management.

"What it has effectively done is transfer all debt to the new company. It should be able to post even higher profits now, given the fact that it remains the power distribution monopoly in the country," another analyst said.

Kenya Power's main problem has been generation of sufficient electricity for the whole country. Imports from neighbouring Uganda has not helped meet the demand for power and Kenya had not contracted two foreign companies to supply power into the main grid on a temporary basis from June this year.
Brokers said the full impact of the expansion was yet to be felt and as such any investment would be for the long term.
"It's very hard to predict our market. The logical thing to expect would be that the price would drop since the bonus dilutes earnings," a broker said.
Kenya Power's market capitalisation stands at about 2.901 billion shillings. It's lowest price was 141 on January 2. The price held at 174 on Thursday.
Brokers predicted a price of 300 shillings per share by end of next month and have taunted investors with special lots at 500 shillings per share but no one has bought at that price.
